title: Clusone to home via Cime di Bares, 5am start
terrain: point-to-point, 20.7km, 1697m D+ / 1244m D-, high point 2108m, descent split 815m + 284m by a 95m re-climb

steps.target: Z1-Z2 approach out of Clusone in the dark, headtorch, 55-84% LTHR
Z2-Z3 sustained climb to ~1890m, ~1150m D+ continuous, 84-89% LTHR
Z1-Z2 ridge and second climb to the 2108m high point, 55-84% LTHR
Z1-Z2 main descent 815m, hike everything over 25%, poles, 55-80% LTHR
Z2 re-climb 95m on trashed quads, RUN this, 80-88% LTHR
Z1-Z2 final descent 284m to the door, 55-80% LTHR

coachNotes: FINAL TRACK, v2, approved 21 Aug. Clusone 652m to home 1104m, 20.7km, 1697m D+, 1244m D-, high point 2108m, start 05:00. Load 185 -> 195 on the extra 2.5km and 163m. V2 IS BETTER THAN V1 AND THE REASON IS THE 95m RE-CLIMB AT km 18.3. It breaks what was a single 932m descent into 815m plus 284m, so the worst continuous eccentric bout drops rather than rises even though total descent goes up 1074 -> 1244m. And climbing 95m on quads that have just absorbed 815m at -20% is the single most race-specific thing in this route: Pirin does exactly that to you late, and a rehearsal that ends on a descent never tests it. RUN THAT RE-CLIMB. Do not hike it because it is small and you are nearly home. If it feels awful, that is the data point you came for. DESCENT GRADIENT IS THE NEW EXPOSURE. km 15-16 is -30% and km 16-17 is -27%, steeper than v1's worst. That is beyond running gradient, so the terrain enforces the hiking rule rather than leaving it to you, which is the honest reason I am comfortable with a bigger day. Working assumption, and it is a moderate-confidence one rather than a certainty: unrunnable-steep hiking loads the quads hard but cycles the knee through the 20-30 degree flexion band far less than a runnable 10-12% descent does, and that band is where the ITB actually gets provoked. So expect sore quads on Sunday and treat lateral knee as the signal that matters. Poles from the high point, short steps, no heel-braking. DESCENT RAMP IS ESSENTIALLY FLAT: 1206m D- on Wednesday to 1244m today, +3%. The number that grew is the climb, which costs nothing eccentric. The site's weekend-D+ flag will fire on 2100 against week 5 and will overstate this day. 05:00 START IS THE RIGHT CALL AND IT SOLVES THE STORM PROBLEM. You top out around 07:45 and are home by 09:35, so the afternoon convective risk that shaped the last three sessions does not apply. Two things it introduces instead. First, headtorch for the first hour: sunrise is about 06:20 and km 1-2 is 21% in the dark, so this is not the section to be casual on. Second, and more important, it breaks the fuelling rehearsal unless you fix it deliberately. BREAKFAST AT 04:15, A REAL ONE. Pirin starts at 08:00 and you will eat at about 05:30, so running this fasted rehearses a race you are not doing. Eat what you intend to eat on race morning, at the same interval before moving, even though 04:15 is unpleasant. Then every 40 minutes from the first climb, race products only, 60-90g carbs per hour, 2 x 500ml minimum. Write down what you actually took and what your stomach did at hour four. This is the whole point of the day. COLD AT THE TOP: 2108m at 07:45 after two hours of sweating on the climb. Carry a layer and put it on at the high point before the descent, not after you are cold on it. NO TIME PRESSURE, car retrieval is not urgent, so the descent is not to be hurried. That is deliberate: the only expensive mistake available today is rushing 30% gradient on tired legs. CLIMB EFFORT 84-89% LTHR, not Z3. You will not climb Pirin's 3300m at Z3. AMBER: any lateral knee signal in the first hour, turn at Monte Pare and take the lower line home, ~800m D+, load 110. Garmin expect 330-400.
